evidence: golden vectors: 9-vector conformance corpus (hop cell incl. batch-coordinate maximum, uplink cell frame, object manifest, three- and eight-operator signed topologies), sealed by a digest over the ordered set, checked in CI against its encoders
cross-architecture: the corpus digest is identical on linux/amd64 and linux/386, so no vector depends on host word size; CI gates on both plus six supported build targets

compatibility matrix: nomad-testnet/conformance/COMPATIBILITY.md covers 57 frozen labels in three groups (document versions with stated refusal behaviour, signature/MAC/digest domain separators, and vendored component labels), enforced by TestCompatibilityMatrixCoversEveryWireVersion which fails naming any version constant the matrix omits

downgrade rule stated normatively: exactly one accepted version per format, an unrecognised version is refused rather than downgraded to, and a change forces a coordinated epoch change; six downgrade cases tested at the topology admission boundary
ambiguity: duplicate JSON keys, trailing content and malformed encodings refused before decoding; mutation and truncation sweeps over every published vector
blockers: the specification is not frozen: docs/PROTOCOL.md describes the protocol but no signed specification tag exists, and tagging needs a project release key that must not be created or held by an agent (see EXTERNAL_BLOCKERS)
state transitions, errors and timeouts are specified per subsystem rather than in one normative document; the matrix covers formats and the downgrade rule, not the full state machine
no conformance schema: the corpus is a JSON file with a fixed shape enforced by its own encoder, not a published schema a second implementation could validate against

evidence: docs/THREAT_MODEL.md: every one of the ten capabilities the criterion names now carries an explicit position (targeted / bounded / not defended), its exclusions, and a pointer to evidence

exclusions stated rather than implied: majority-compromised committee, dense coded pollution, availability under sustained loss, fair allocation under Sybil, whole-binary egress, long-horizon intersection
blockers: review by a party that did not author the document. The artifact is complete; what is missing is the word 'reviewed' in the criterion. The author of THREAT_MODEL.md and CLAIM_TEST_MATRIX.md must not be the one who judges them adequate, per the project's implementer/evaluator rule. This does not require external independence (PROD-04 and PROD-29 are the criteria that do), only a second party.

evidence: canonical encodings: signed documents are verified by re-serialising what was parsed, so identity is the canonical form rather than the received bytes; TestAmbiguousJSONRepresentationsAreRefusedOrCanonical asserts that reordering, re-indentation and trailing whitespace either fail or map to the identical digest

ambiguity fails closed: live/strictjson refuses a duplicate JSON key at any depth, plus malformed input and a second document after the first, and runs before decoding in both topology.Verify and batch.VerifyDescriptor. mutation and truncation: every sampled prefix and every sampled single-bit flip of every published vector must be refused (live/conformance/differential_test.go)

log scraping: a production node runs with known secrets and every file under its state directory is scanned in raw, hex, upper hex and three base64 forms, with the instrument rehearsed against all five secrets first

crash data: GOTRACEBACK=none on every compose service, verified against a real panicking process built under testdata -- no goroutine dump, no frame arguments, no secret. The in-process debug.SetTraceback("none") was measured to be inert and replaced; see the finding in EVIDENCE_INDEX
a compose test fails any service that declares its own environment without repeating GOTRACEBACK, which is how the three DKG services were caught silently dropping it via YAML merge semantics
